text:
Rebuttal to the misinformation campaign on ISTS applicability

In continuation of the misinformation campaign against the
arrangement with SECI, the TDP and its affiliated media allege that
the burden on ISTS (Inter-Sate Transmission System) charges on
the distribution utilities of Andhra Pradesh owing to the solar
power procurement from SECI would be unsustainably high.

The truth has been made public several times in the past regarding
the non-applicability of ISTS charges to the arrangement with
SECI. However, in the light of the intensification of the
misinformation campaign, the facts are once again being placed
before the public. The extracts of the relevant documents and a
brief explanation of its contents are provided below.

- The SECI has made an offer to the AP State Government vide
its letter dated 15ᵗʰ September, 2021 and in the letter the
SECI, a Government of India undertaking clearly specified
that the Government of India, as a special incentive granted
ISTS waiver to this proposal irrespective of the
commissioning date of the project. Further, the letter clearly
states that **no such charges** would be applicable on
Government of Andhra Pradesh. (**Copy of the SECI letter is**
**enclosed**)

- Realizing the importance of the ISTS charges waiver for the
whole transaction, the offer letter from SECI conveying the
Government of India’s ISTS charges waiver as a special
incentive and the notification from Ministry of Power,

text:
Government of India providing for the ISTS charges waiver
are made part of the PSA (Power Supply Agreement) signed
amongst the parties, distribution utilities of Andhra Pradesh,
Government of Andhra Pradesh and the Solar Energy
Corporation of India Limited. (**Copy of the PSA with SECI is**
**enclosed**)

- The Ministry of Power, Government of India, has through
notification dated 30ᵗʰ November 2021 has made an
inclusion in the Ministry of Power, Government of India’s
Order No. 23/12/2016 – R&R dated 23ʳᵈ November, 2021,
providing for waiver of inter-state transmission charges on
transmission of electricity from solar and wind sources of
energy. The 30ᵗʰ November, 2021 notification inclusion
conveys that, ISTS charges shall be waived for Solar PV plants
commissioned under SECI tender for manufacturing linked
capacity scheme (RFS No. SECI/C&P/Rfs/2GW
Manufacturing/P-3/R1/062019 dated 25.06.2019) for sale to
entities having RPO, irrespective of whether this power is
within RPO or not. (**Copy of Ministry of Power notification**
**dated 30ᵗʰ November, 2021 is enclosed**)

- The Ministry of Power, Government of India’s earlier
notification dated 15ᵗʰ January 2021 also provides that Solar
PV plants commissioned under SECI tender for
manufacturing linked capacity scheme (RFS No.
SECI/C&P/Rfs/2GW Manufacturing/P-3/R1/062019 dated
25.06.2019) for sale to entities having RPO, irrespective of
whether this power is within RPO or not, is providing ISTS

waiver. (Copy of Ministry of Power notification dated 15th ,

- The CERC’s (Central Electricity Regulatory Commission)
notification dated 7ᵗʰ February, 2023, referred to as CERC
(sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses)
(First Amendment) Regulations 2023 made the express
stipulation that, generation from PV generating stations
under SECI manufacturing linked capacity scheme (RFS No.
SECI/C&P/Rfs/2GW Manufacturing/P-3/R1/062019 dated
25.06.2019) for sale to entities having RPO irrespective of
the date of COD of such generating station shall be
considered for the waiver of transmission charges for a
period of 25 years from the date of COD. (**Copy of the**
**relevant page from the CERC notification is enclosed**)

Despite several notifications from the Ministry of Power,
Government of India, the Central Electricity Regulatory
Authority’s regulations providing for ISTS waiver, SECI, a
Government of India undertaking stipulating the ISTS waiver for
the power supply arrangement and making it a part of the binding
contract amongst the parties, the TDP and their affiliated media
continue to spread lies.
